The kernel compiled, passed all 5 correctness trials, and is about 16% faster than the reference `nn.ConvTranspose3d` on this hardware (90 ms vs 107 ms mean).

The implementation in [output_model_new.py](/root/lumen-clean/lumen-sosp26-ae-origin/runs/kernelbench_generation_level1_moonbridge_no_examples/p72/round0/output_model_new.py) uses a single `@avelang.jit` kernel with an output-driven gather approach: each thread computes one output element by iterating over the 3D kernel volume, checking the stride-divisibility condition (`(d_out + pad - kd) % stride == 0`) with integer arithmetic to determine whether an input element contributes, then accumulating in FP32 from BF16 inputs and weights. The grid is a flat 1D launch over all `B * OC * D_out * H_out * W_out` output elements with 256-thread blocks. Groups, bias, and output-padding are all handled correctly.
